title: Cost-economy safety scorer and human-audit pipeline for batching/caching recommendations
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Objective: Build an automated scoring and human-audit pipeline that assesses the semantic and safety impact of batching/caching configuration recommendations before they are applied to production. The scorer should produce a compact risk score for each recommended config (0-100) along with a small set of rationale signals and a prioritized list of reference prompts that most likely surface regressions.

Scope and constraints:
- Input: a candidate config change (batch size / cache policy / prefix prefetch spec), the model variant(s) it targets, and a stratified sample of recent real requests grouped by workload signature.
- Output: risk_score, failing_prompt_examples (<=20), signal_breakdown (semantic-delta, hallucination-likelihood, latency-impact, distribution-shift), stable-anchor flag, and human_review_reasoning tokens.
- Must run within the staging acceptance window (target 15m wall-clock for a full run on 10k sample requests using offline compute).
- Integrate with our canary apply flow: if risk_score > 55 then block automated apply; if 35 < risk_score <= 55 then require human sign-off; below 35 allow auto-apply with audit log.

Design notes:
- Semantic fidelity measurement: use ensemble of embedding-cosine deltas (cosine to baseline outputs), a lightweight LM-based divergence scorer (KL proxy over next-token logits sampled from baseline vs candidate), and classification heuristics for instruction-following failures.
- Safety heuristics: reuse existing safety models but add a delta-check to detect increases in safety-risk labels vs baseline. Flag rare but high-severity categories for immediate human review.
- Golden/reference prompts: do not rely on a single golden set. Instead compute a ranked reference prompt set per workload slice by frequency * sensitivity (i.e., prompts that historically change outputs when batching/caching changes). These are called "canonical-check prompts" in this ticket.
- Human review UX: produce a compact review card with 6 side-by-side output diffs, short automated summary (one-sentence delta), and a checkbox checklist (semantic acceptable, no new hallucinations, latency within SLO).

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline implemented and wired into the staging canary flow.
- Scorer produces reproducible risk_score within +/- 3 points on repeated runs over same sample.
- Human review card renders in console with artifact links and allows sign-off/deny with comments.
- Integration tests cover three synthetic regressions (prompt truncation, prefix collision, kv-cache-dup) and detect them at defined thresholds.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy scoring pipeline in shadow mode for a week, logging scores and reviewer picks (no enforcement).
2) Run an internal audit (small cross-team panel) on 50 shadowed changes. Tune thresholds.
3) Soft-enforce blocking policy for P1 configs with risk_score > 65 for two weeks.
4) Full enforcement with automated apply/rollback hooks after threshold stability verified.

Notes on uniqueness: This ticket prioritizes a compact risk-scoring abstraction that can be interpreted by engineers and Product owners and avoids relying purely on static golden anchors. It emphasizes workload-aware canonical prompt selection and a human-in-the-loop review card rather than long golden corpora or single anchor prompts.

comments: 2025-01-20 - Aisha Raman: Kickoff meeting notes attached to Confluence design doc. Agreed on ensemble approach for semantic fidelity (embeddings + next-token proxy). Marcus to own implementation of the delta aggregator.

2025-01-25 - Marcus Li: Implemented first-pass scorer that computes embedding cosine delta and a simple token-level edit-distance heuristic. Runs against 2k sample requests in ~9 minutes offline. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1872

2025-01-30 - Priya Singh (PM): Reviewed UX mockups. Requested that human review card include a one-line natural language summary generated by the eval pipeline. Added label 'human-audit' and requested 3 example diffs be shown by default.
2025-02-03 - Security review (Alex Kim): Confirmed no new data exfiltration risk; suggested we redact PII in example prompts. Added task to include automated PII scrub step in preprocessing.

2025-02-07 - Engineering: Added safety-delta checks using the existing safety classifier. Several low-frequency false positives observed on internal privacy prompts; opened ENG-990123 to investigate classifier calibration.

2025-02-11 - Marcus Li: Shadow run results uploaded to dashboard. Summary: out of 143 candidate configs, 11 had risk_score > 55, 6 of those were true regressions per human audit panel, 5 were false alarms (precision ~55%). Adjusted threshold recommendation to 50 for sign-off and 65 for block and filed follow-ups for improving precision. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/cost-scorer/shadow-2025?panel=summary

2025-02-12 - Aisha Raman: Planning retrospective scheduled for 2025-02-18 to decide on threshold tuning and automation gating. Next steps: refine canonical-check prompt selector, add PII scrub, expand synthetic regression battery, and tighten safety-classifier calibration.
